chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad or someone else, from Ali ibn Hadid, from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
'Most of those who die from among our followers (die) from rapid abdominal illness.'

key_terms.الْبَطَنِ الذَّرِيعِ: Rapid/swift abdominal illness — typically interpreted as severe diarrhea or dysentery
key_terms.مَوَالِينَا: Our followers/those under our Wilayah — the Shia who hold spiritual allegiance to the Imams

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about the cause of death of most Shia believers?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) observed that the majority of deaths among the Shia — those who hold Wilayah of the Imams — occur due to acute gastrointestinal ailments (al-batan al-dhari'). This statement is recorded in the chapter on causes of death in al-Kafi. Scholars have interpreted this as a descriptive observation about the prevalent health conditions among the Shia community of that era, and some have seen it as an implicit honor — that believers die from illness rather than in battle as enemies.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammd, or someone else, from Ali Bin Hadeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Most of the dying ones, from those who are in our<sup>asws</sup> Wilayah, (are dying) by abdominal illnesses’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad or someone other than him from Ali ibn Hadid from who has said the following: “Al-Rida, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
most of our followers die from widespread stomach (internal) illness.”
